title: the_seed_swap
display_title: My neighbor swapped my late dad's tomato seeds for store-bought ones — she doesn't know I know
beats: My neighbor (61F) has been "helping" me garden every spring since my dad died and left me his tomato seeds.
Those seeds were the last thing he ever grew — forty years of saving them from his own plants, one jar, never sold, never shared.
This year she offered to "start them early" in her greenhouse so I wouldn't have to bother.
The seedlings came back three weeks later, healthy, labeled, exactly on schedule — but the leaves were the wrong shape.
I checked the jar she returned: it was full again, but the seeds inside were smooth and uniform, nothing like Dad's wrinkled, uneven ones.
I haven't said anything to her yet — I just water them every day and wait to see what actually grows.
What would you do if you found out before the harvest?
